title: ×1.50-at-min-window-1152×648 AC ("layout clamps, AC-pinned") has no exercising path — harness renders only at 1280×720
evidence: Spec I/O matrix row: "| Scale ×1.50 at min window 1152×648 | panel stepper | top band (health card, forecast, crisis banner), QoS panel, tray, caption strip never overlap | layout clamps, AC-pinned |"; harness/main.odin:266: "	rl.InitWindow(1280, 720, "pp-harness")"; demos/a11y_scale.dem:5: "a11y scale 150"; golden-manifest.txt: "a11y_scale.dem runs at UI scale x1.50 (a11y scale 150) with its own fresh goldens"; only 1152/648 occurrences in the repo are app/main.odin:33-34 "MIN_WIN_W :: 1152" / "MIN_WIN_H :: 648" (runtime SetWindowMinSize clamp, no test)
detail: The spec's min-window overlap AC claims to be pinned, but every golden/parity/palcheck path runs at fixed 1280×720. HUD overlap regressions at ×1.50/1152×648 would pass all 10 CI gates silently.
recommended_fix: Add a harness render size (or a dedicated 1152×648 ×1.50 demo/golden, or a rect-overlap unit test over the hud()-scaled surfaces) so the min-window AC is mechanically pinned.

title: palcheck oracle selects the 40-vs-48 threshold by color-value equality on pr[0] only, not pair identity — a future signal/map token collision silently relaxes the check
detail: The map threshold is inferred from the pair's first color matching a map-token VALUE. If a future mode edit sets any signal token (state/lane/pipe/class) equal to water/park/coast/canvas, that signal pair silently falls under the looser 40 threshold (and pr[0]==p.canvas is reachable only via such a collision — no shipped pair starts with canvas).
recommended_fix: Tag each pair signal/map at construction (e.g. append a bool alongside the pair) and branch the threshold on the tag instead of color-value equality.

title: Input parity is never exercised under an active a11y mode — the parity view always loads the default palette with mode Off, motion on, ×1.00
evidence:
harness/parity.odin:182-183 (drive_parity): "	pal := rnd.palette_load()
	view.palette = &pal"; harness/parity.odin:928-929 (run_input_parity): "	pal := rnd.palette_load()
	view.palette = &pal"; grep for ui_scale/reduced_motion/palette_apply in harness/parity.odin returns nothing; epic-7-context.md: "Full input parity (mouse/touch/controller) holds under every a11y mode; no input-dependent mechanics."
detail: The epic contract "parity holds under every a11y mode" has no driving path: no scenario applies palette_apply_mode/ui_scale/reduced_motion to the parity view, so mode-dependent surfaces (e.g. the mode-dependent settings_chip_rect width) go untested.
recommended_fix: Add a parity pass (or scenario variant) that applies each a11y mode to the view before driving the device frames, asserting identical command streams.

title: Settings-panel parity asserts only panel_open; end panel_row diverges by device by construction and is never compared
evidence:
Scenario: mouse = "evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .S}),
			evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .Down}),
		evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .Enter}),
		evs(inp.Key_Press{key = .S})" vs touch = "evs(inp.Touch_Press{pos = {chip.x + chip.width / 2, chip.y + chip.height / 2}}),
			evs(inp.Touch_Press{pos = {row0.x + row0.width / 2, row0.y + row0.height / 2}}),..."; check_states case "input_parity_settings_panel": "for i in 0 ..< len(devs) {
			if runs[i].panel_open {
				append(fails, ...)"; panel_row is stored into Parity_Run (line 246) but compared nowhere
detail: Mouse/pad navigate Down to row 1 before closing; touch only focuses row 0 — end panel_row differs across devices (1 vs 0). The PR claim "identical end input-state" is only partially pinned (panel_open only); row-focus divergence would go undetected.
recommended_fix: Either align the touch script to navigate to the same row before closing, or additionally assert runs[i].panel_row equality across devices in check_states.
